2609.21811.title: MIST: Multimodal Survival Prediction with Genomic-Guided Histology Attention
2609.21811.paper_summary: Multimodal survival models can combine complementary prognostic information from whole-slide images and genomic profiles, but effective fusion remains challenging amid external cohort shift and computational complexity. To address these challenges, we propose MIST, multimodal survival prediction with genomic-guided histology attention. MIST represents genomic features as tokens and allows them to query compact foundation-model-derived histology context tokens before survival prediction. This design enriches molecular information with histology context rather than merging separately encoded modalities only at the final stage. Training combines discrete-time survival prediction with genomic feature masking, WSI dropout, and paired WSI-genomics contrastive alignment. Across four external evaluations in colon, renal, lung, and glioblastoma cohorts, MIST improves external C-index over standard fusion baselines in the primary comparisons. These results support genomic-guided histology attention as a compact and effective strategy for multimodal oncology outcome prediction. Our code is available at https://github.com/samiyavuuz/MIST .
2609.21811.paper_summary_zh: 多模態生存模型可以結合來自全片影像和基因組特徵的互補預後信息，但在外部隊列轉移和計算複雜性中，有效融合仍然具有挑戰性。為了解決這些挑戰，我們提出了 MIST，即基因組引導的組織學注意的多模態生存預測。MIST 將基因組特徵表示為標記，並允許它們在生存預測之前查詢由基礎模型衍生的組織學上下文標記。這種設計通過組織學上下文豐富分子信息，而不是僅在最終階段合併單獨編碼的模態。訓練結合了離散時間生存預測、基因組特徵遮罩、WSI 隨機失活和配對的 WSI-基因組對比對齊。在結腸、腎臟、肺部和膠質母細胞瘤隊列的四個外部評估中，MIST 在主要比較中改善了外部 C 指數，超過了標準融合基準。這些結果支持基因組引導的組織學注意作為多模態腫瘤結果預測的一種緊湊而有效的策略。我們的代碼可在 https://github.com/samiyavuuz/MIST 獲得。
